en.content:
If AB<sub>4</sub> molecule is a polar molecule, a possible
geometry of AB<sub>4</sub> is

options.content: Tetrahedral
Rectangular planar
Square pyramidal
Square planar

en.explanation:
An molecule is polar only if its four A–B bond dipoles do not cancel.

  • Tetrahedral: the four equal A–B dipoles point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron and cancel, so the molecule is non-polar (e.g. , ).

  • Rectangular planar and square planar: every A–B dipole has an equal one pointing the opposite way (at ), so they cancel and both shapes are non-polar (e.g. is square planar).

  • Square pyramidal: A sits at the apex above the square of four B atoms. The components of the four dipoles in the plane of the base cancel, but their components along the axis all point the same way and add up, so the molecule has a net dipole moment and is polar.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
